note: Every name carries a signed edge_score on -100..+100. There is no call and no threshold: rank on edge_score and cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what makes the ranking question answerable at every k.

findings.finding: NSSF-adjusted NICS for SWBI's exact fiscal Q1 (May+June+July 2026) totalled 3,290,647 against 3,055,402 a year earlier, +7.70% y/y - a 6.5-point acceleration from the +1.20% in the Feb-Apr quarter on which SWBI just printed revenue +26.7% and handgun sell-in +23.2%, while consensus looks for only +16% revenue growth off an $85.1M base.
findings.adversary_note: Every input is published, and published loudly. The NSSF-adjusted NICS series is released monthly by NSSF and headlined within days by the entire firearms trade press: the July figure of 1,061,883 / +8.5% y/y was carried by Outdoor Wire, OutdoorHub, NRA Women, GunsAmerica, Ammoland and TheFirearmBlog in the first half of August. The github CSV cited here is a third-party mirror, not a private dataset. The Feb-Apr comparator is in SWBI's own 2026-06-17 release ('handgun unit sales into the sporting goods channel increasing 23.2%... while NICS increased only 1.1%'), and the +16% consensus off an $85.1M base is in a StockStory preview syndicated to Yahoo on 2026-09-01 (consensus revenue $98.7M). What is genuinely unpublished is only the three-month sum aligned to SWBI's fiscal quarter and the framing as a '6.5-point acceleration' - trivial arithmetic on a headline series that four covering analysts model explicitly. And the claim's own internal evidence undercuts it: SWBI printed +26.7% revenue against NICS +1.1%, so the series has almost no explanatory power for SWBI shipments, which makes +7.7% a weak lever on a print already guided to +15-20%. Decisive tape point: each of the three monthly releases landed before today and SWBI fell through all of them - $14.76 on 2026-08-03 to $12.47 on 2026-09-03 - while RGR was flat over the same window. Either the market saw the data and discounted it, or it is pricing something SWBI-specific.

findings.finding: Both channel layers turned positive in SWBI's exact quarter, and both datapoints were published after SWBI last spoke: Ruger's distributor inventories fell 45,800 units and finished goods 100,100 units on sell-through +19% (2026-07-29), and Sportsman's Warehouse's 10-Q for the 13 weeks ended 2026-08-01 shows firearm sales +$5.2M / +8.7% and ammunition +$3.9M / +9.9% (filed 2026-09-01).
findings.adversary_note: Both halves are in the wire, and one of them is in SWBI-specific pre-print wire copy. Ruger's Q2 release of 2026-07-29 (net sales $158.1M, +19%) was on BusinessWire, Yahoo and Las Vegas Sun the same day, the call transcript was on Motley Fool by 2026-08-07, and - decisively - a StockStory SWBI earnings preview syndicated to Yahoo on 2026-09-01 already draws the read-across explicitly: 'Ruger delivered 19.3% year-on-year revenue growth, beating analyst expectations by 23%... could provide a positive read-across for the firearm industry.' The SPWH half is the same day's press release and call as the 10-Q (globenewswire 2026-09-01, transcript on Investing.com, stocktitan, Manila Times), with 'firearms up 8% and ammunition up nearly 11%' quoted in the coverage; the 10-Q's +8.7%/+9.9% category detail is a second reading of the same quarter, not a second fact. The only real residual is the specific channel-inventory framing (-45,800 distributor / -100,100 finished-goods units) and its 'shipments run ahead of retail' implication, which is standard sector analysis rather than a discovery. Note the SWBI tape gave the SPWH print nothing: +0.08% on 2026-09-02, the day after.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-05 the N.D. Texas entered final judgment and a permanent injunction in Silencer Shop Foundation v. ATF holding NFA registration of suppressors/SBRs/SBSs unconstitutional after the tax went to zero; the stay expired 2026-08-12 and DOJ declined an emergency appeal - three weeks after SWBI's 2026-07-15 investor day told investors suppressors were its fastest-growing lane at +95.6% revenue growth in H1 CY2026 into a $700M-$950M TAM, with July NFA-category NICS checks +108.8% y/y to 130,013.
findings.adversary_note: This is mainstream news, not an obscure docket entry. Judge Hendrix's 2026-08-05 judgment in the consolidated Silencer Shop Foundation v. ATF / Jensen v. ATF was covered the same day by NRA-ILA, then by Wiley's client alert, NSSF's own compliance guidance, SilencerCo, Silencer Central, Silencer Shop, the American Suppressor Association and Concealed Carry Inc, and by NPR on 2026-08-17 - it is the largest change to suppressor law since 1934 and was reported as such. The stay expiry on 2026-08-12 and DOJ's non-appeal were themselves the subject of dedicated NRA-ILA Q&A pieces on 08-12 and 08-17. The SWBI investor-day figures paired with it (+95.6% suppressor revenue growth in H1 CY2026, $700M-$950M TAM) come from a Reg FD 8-K exhibit filed 2026-07-15 - a public company filing, and I verified both figures in it directly. Two further discounts: the ruling is dated 2026-08-05, five days after SWBI's fiscal quarter ended 2026-07-31, so it cannot touch a single dollar of the reported numbers and can only enter through tonight's commentary; and it is genuinely two-sided - taking suppressors off the NFA expands volume but also destroys the paperwork friction and dealer-network moat that let incumbents earn on the category, and invites competition into a segment where SWBI has never disclosed a revenue dollar. Against $523.8M FY26 revenue, a category SWBI declines to size is not a large lever even doubling.

findings.finding: SWBI's Q1 FY27 guide of +15-20% revenue was given 2026-06-17 with only May adjusted NICS (+3.2% y/y) published; June came in +11.7% (1,123,006 vs 1,004,986) and July +8.5% (1,061,883 vs 978,731), so the two months the guide could not see were 3-4x stronger than the one it could, and the quarter-aligned May-July industry number is +7.7% y/y (3,290,647 vs 3,055,402).
findings.adversary_note: The sharpest claim in the brief and the one I can least easily find published - I searched for any note observing that SWBI's 2026-06-17 guide was set with only the May NICS print visible and found none. The underlying facts are all public (the +15-20% Q1 guide is in the Q4 call transcript on Investing.com; the three monthly NICS figures are in trade press) but the information-set argument is not drawn anywhere. Three real discounts. First, the source is misdated for part of the claim: the cited Outdoor Wire URL is /releases/2026/07/, the June release published 2026-07-06, and it cannot contain the July figure - the July release lives at /releases/2026/08/. Second, the mechanism assumes SWBI guides off industry NICS, when the company's own last print showed +26.7% revenue against NICS +1.1% and management guides off its order book and shipment plan; a manufacturer three weeks into its own quarter already knows its June shipments better than any NICS reading. Third, the street is already at +16% against a 15-20% guide, i.e. barely above the low end, so the guide's conservatism is at least partly reflected and a beat to the top end is a ~2.5% revenue surprise, not a step change. And the tape has had every monthly release: the stock is 16.4% lower than when the guide was given.

findings.finding: NFA (suppressor/SBR) background checks are exploding after the 1-Jan-2026 elimination of the $200 tax stamp - June 2026 166,677 (+177.1% y/y) and July 2026 130,013 (+108.8%) - and SWBI's own Reg FD Investor Day deck filed 2026-07-15 discloses suppressor revenue +95.6% in the first six months of calendar 2026 against a US category it sizes at $700-950m; the June/July NFA data postdates the window that 95.6% covers, so the current run rate is higher than the only figure the company has published.
findings.adversary_note: The NFA-check surge is the trade-press headline, not a buried line: Ammoland's August piece is literally titled 'July Gun Sales Rise 8.5% as NFA Checks More Than Double', and the July NFA figure of 130,013 / +108.8% appears in the NSSF release itself and in every monthly recap. The 95.6% suppressor growth and the $700-950M TAM are in SWBI's own 8-K exhibit filed 2026-07-15, which I verified line by line. The residual - that June/July NFA data postdates the H1 window the 95.6% covers, so the current run rate is higher - is a legitimate inference and I find it nowhere, but it is an inference on two published series that a reader of both would reach in a minute. The binding problem is size, not novelty: SWBI has never disclosed a suppressor revenue dollar (the deck gives a growth rate and a category TAM and no company figure), the segment is small enough that the company chose not to size it, and FY26 revenue was $523.8M. Doubling something unsized is not obviously worth much, and half of the June/July NFA surge sits inside the reported quarter anyway, meaning it is already implicitly inside the +15-20% guide the company reaffirmed nothing against.

findings.finding: Sportsman's Warehouse reported its quarter ended 2026-08-01 on 2026-09-01 - two days before SWBI prints and covering almost exactly SWBI's May-July fiscal Q1 - with hunting and shooting sports same-store sales +6.7%, and CEO Paul Stone saying on the call 'Firearms up 8% and ammo is up nearly 11% on the Q'; the stock rose 9.2% after hours.
findings.adversary_note: This is a public-company earnings release from two days ago with wide same-day pickup - GlobeNewswire, Manila Times, StockTitan, MarketBeat, Cerbat Gem, and an Investing.com transcript recap headlined 'tops Q2 2026 estimates, shares jump' that carries the exact firearms/ammo category numbers. The CEO quote is from a public call. Nothing here is unpublished; the claim is an inference from a published print. What holds the number down from the 80s is that the read-across was demonstrably not paid for in SWBI: the day after SPWH's release SWBI closed +0.08%, and the one SWBI-specific pre-print preview I can find (StockStory, syndicated to Yahoo 2026-09-01) names Ruger and Clarus as comparables and does not mention Sportsman's Warehouse at all. So the fact is fully public but the specific SWBI channel has not been drawn in wire copy, and the tape shows no bid. Also note SPWH's headline was flat total comps on +0.6% sales - a retailer whose overall print was mediocre, with strength confined to two categories, is a softer read-through than the framing implies, and SPWH's +9.2% move was about its own EBITDA and margin, not about firearm units.

findings.finding: Ruger's 8-K for the coincident Apr-Jun 2026 quarter reports net sales $158.1m, +19% y/y, sell-through +19% against adjusted NICS +5%, and distributors' inventories down 45,800 units y/y - the channel manufacturers ship into is lean, which is the condition under which factory shipments run ahead of retail demand rather than behind it.
findings.adversary_note: This is the most priced claim in the brief. Ruger's Q2 release went out on BusinessWire on 2026-07-29 and was picked up the same day by Yahoo Finance, Las Vegas Sun and Quiver; the call transcript was on Motley Fool and the Globe and Mail by 2026-08-07; and the read-across to SWBI specifically is in pre-print wire copy - the StockStory preview syndicated to Yahoo on 2026-09-01 states that 'Ruger delivered 19.3% year-on-year revenue growth, beating analyst expectations by 23%, and traded up 3.3%,' adding that this 'could provide a positive read-across for the firearm industry.' Peer read-across from the only other listed pure-play firearm manufacturer, five weeks before the print, is the single most standard thing a sector analyst does; the lean-channel interpretation is textbook. It is also arithmetically the weakest lever of the bullish cluster: Ruger's channel is Ruger's channel, SWBI's own last release said channel inventory of its handguns was essentially unchanged, and Ruger's beat was ASP- and new-product-driven (ASP +10% to $384), which is company-specific execution rather than an industry shipment condition.

findings.finding: I can find no company-specific cause for the 16.4% 20-day de-rating: SWBI's only SEC filings since the 17-Jun print are a 7.01 investor-day deck (2026-07-15) and the routine FY26 annual report to shareholders (2026-08-06, a PDF-only submission), with zero Form 4s between 2026-08-01 and 2026-09-03 and no 8-K under items 1.01, 2.03, 5.02 or 8.01.
findings.adversary_note: I checked this one and the factual core survives: I can find no SWBI-specific news in August 2026 other than the routine 2026-08-20 earnings-date alert and the FY26 annual report to shareholders, no analyst action I can date to August, and the daily tape shows no discrete gap - $14.76 on 08-03 grinding to $12.47 on 09-03 with the largest single day only -3.19%. That is real and it is unpublished as an observation. But as a *finding* it has two problems that put it near the middle rather than the bottom. First, an absence of filings is not information the market lacks - EDGAR is public, and the market is the entity that sold the stock down; nobody is mispricing SWBI because they failed to check for an 8-K. Second, and more damaging, the absence of a filed cause is not the absence of a cause, and the cross-section says something SWBI-specific is happening: over 08-19 to 09-03 RGR went $38.20 to $38.32, flat, while SWBI fell 11.7%. A steady 1-3% daily bleed on ordinary volume with an idiosyncratic 12-point underperformance of the closest peer is the signature of estimate cuts, a persistent seller, or informed positioning - and it cuts against the rest of this brief rather than with it, because it means the market has had every bullish datapoint in the other seven claims and de-rated anyway. There is also no directional mechanism attached: 'unexplained decline' does not become 'will rally on the print'. The one thing that mildly supports the claim is the option market's indifference - 25d skew -0.67 with calls marginally bid and put/call OI 0.70 - which says the sellers were not buying protection against a bad print.

findings.finding: Asana's live production API now licenses AI Studio as a per-user seat with three tiers - ai_studio_plus, ai_studio_pro and ai_studio_max - of which 'Max' appears nowhere on Asana's public pricing page or help docs, and every AI run is tagged with a credit_source of 'paid' or 'free'; this is the recurring, seat-priced AI line management pre-committed on the Q1 call to quantify for the first time on THIS call.
findings.source_date: 2026-09-03 (retrieved; the endpoint was announced 2026-07-02 per Asana's changelog)
findings.adversary_note: The commercial event this claim points to - Asana quantifying AI Studio / AI product contribution on THIS call - is not novel: on the Q1 FY27 call (2026-05-28) management explicitly said it 'plans to provide a more comprehensive update on AI product contribution during its second-quarter call,' and already disclosed AI product bookings at 17% of net-new ARR vs a 15% FY target. That pre-commitment is in every transcript recap, so the market is already positioned for an AI number this print. The specific evidence the hunter adds - an API enum (ai_studio_plus/pro/max, credit_source paid/free) - is plumbing, not revenue: an enum value proves a tier can be represented in the data model, not that 'Max' is sold, priced, or contributing material ARR. 'Max appears nowhere on the pricing page' is equally consistent with an unlaunched or internal tier as with a stealth premium SKU. So the narrative is priced and the incremental enum evidence does not establish the commercial magnitude being inferred.

findings.finding: Asana retired 7,368,000 shares for $44.985 million in the single quarter ended 2026-04-30 - roughly 3% of shares outstanding in three months at an average of about $6.11 - leaving $154.5 million authorised, against a float already shrunk by Moskovitz's ~27% stake and short interest above 22%.
findings.adversary_note: The repurchase is fully public and old: the 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-04-30 (filed 2026-05-28) discloses $45.0m / 7.4m shares at ~$6.11 and ~$155m remaining, and Asana separately announced a $100m expansion of the program - all reported by stocktitan and TipRanks months ago. Short interest above 22% and Moskovitz's ~27% stake are standing structural facts, not new information; 'age is not novelty.' The buyback-support / thin-float thesis is a well-worn part of this name's bull case and has had a full quarter to be absorbed. The shares bought were at $6.11 against a $10.30 spot, so the marginal support at current prices is modest and the remaining authorization is a known quantity.

findings.finding: monday.com's Q2 print on 2026-08-10 - the first category datapoint issued after Asana last spoke, covering a quarter that overlaps two thirds of Asana's - reported NDR of 109%, 'gross retention is also at historical highs' and 'we are still seeing a double-digit seat growth year-over-year in enterprise', directly contradicting the seat-destruction frame that caps Asana's multiple.
findings.adversary_note: monday.com's Q2 print (2026-08-10) is public and heavily reported - NDR 109%, gross retention at highs, double-digit enterprise seat growth - and every ASAN-covering analyst had three-plus weeks to fold that category read into estimates before this print. The read-across is also contestable, which limits its force: MNDY grew revenue 22% vs ASAN's ~9%, MNDY shares actually fell premarket on its beat, and a healthier competitor arguably signals share loss for ASAN as easily as a healthy category. So the datapoint is published and the bullish 'seat destruction is overdone' inference is an analyst-level interpretation, not proprietary - but the specific cross-read to ASAN's own multiple is not drawn out anywhere explicitly, leaving some residual.

findings.finding: Asana enters this print with no dedicated chief accounting officer: CAO/PAO Veronica Sosa resigned on 2026-07-13 effective 2026-08-07, and on 2026-08-26 - six days before the print - the board handed the principal accounting officer role to CFO Aziz Megji, himself appointed only in March 2026 after CFO Sonalee Parekh resigned in February 2026, making three finance-leadership changes in six months.
findings.adversary_note: The 8-K handing the PAO role to CFO Megji is public (filed 2026-08-28, event 2026-08-26) and was covered by stocktitan, and every earlier leg - Sosa's March appointment, her July resignation, the Parekh-to-Megji CFO transition - was individually disclosed and reported. Crucially the filings state there were no disagreements and no issues with accounting policies or practices, which deflates the governance-risk inference the claim draws. The market's own reaction is dispositive here: rather than sell on the 08-26 news, ASAN rose ~8.9% on 08-29 into the print, so the tape treated the finance-leadership churn as immaterial. Governance turnover of this kind rarely reaches an earnings-print move absent a restatement, which no source alleges.

findings.finding: After a 16.8% twenty-day run-up that contemporaneous coverage attributes to short covering and sector rotation rather than company news, ASAN trades roughly 10% ABOVE the 15-analyst average price target of $9.27 with a consensus 'Hold', and consensus FY27 revenue of $860.8m sits dead centre of the company's own $855.5-863.5m guide - so there is no estimate slack to beat into.
findings.adversary_note: This finding is a description of the consensus, not information hidden from it. The $9.27 average target, the Hold rating (4 Buy / 8 Hold / 2 Sell), the ~10% premium of spot over target, and consensus FY27 revenue of $860.8m sitting dead-center of the company's own $855.5-863.5m guide are all published on public forecast pages and in a TradingView note, timestamped the morning of the print. 'Consensus is dead-center of guidance with no slack' is the priced state by definition - it restates the setup every participant already sees. The run-up's attribution to short covering / rotation rather than fundamentals is likewise in contemporaneous coverage.

findings.finding: The two inputs nobody watching MAMA is tracking are benign in exactly this quarter: CME 40-lb block cheddar closed $1.5050/lb on 2026-07-08, near the bottom of its own 2022-2026 $1.30-$2.40 range, and retail boneless chicken breast averaged $4.15/lb in July 2026, down 1.2% year over year with breast-meat supply called balanced-to-heavy through end-2026 - so the Q1 gross-margin shortfall the market de-rated the stock for, which the CFO quantified on the June 8 call as ~$0.5-1.0m of one-time launch labour/material inefficiency plus ~$0.5m reclassified from marketing to trade, was not a commodity problem and does not have a commodity reason to repeat.
findings.adversary_note: The conclusion of this claim - that the Q1 gross-margin shortfall was one-time launch inefficiency and not a commodity problem, so margins revert to the mid-to-high 20s - is management's own publicly stated guidance from the June 8 call, echoed across every earnings summary (StockTitan, GuruFocus, Yahoo, Motley Fool). The CFO explicitly quantified the ~$0.5-1.0m one-time labour/material inefficiency and the ~$0.5m marketing-to-trade reclass, and guided margins back to target 'as new product launches transition from startup phase to steady-state.' The market has had this since June 8. What is genuinely obscure and unpriced is the commodity leg itself - CME block cheddar at $1.505 near the bottom of its range and boneless breast at $4.15/lb - which no MAMA-facing coverage connects; but that is a secondary confirmation of an already-published margin-recovery thesis, not the driver, and cheese/chicken were never the reason the market de-rated the stock.

findings.finding: Fiscal Q2 (May 1 - Jul 31 2026) is the first full quarter of revenue from the 2,000 Walmart and 750 Target deli doors, which management said on 2026-06-08 'did not launch till the middle to end of April - so we had all the costs... The cost is all in Q1. But really, very little of the revenue was in Q1' - i.e. the costs and the revenue were split across the quarter boundary in the company's favour, and the market has sold the stock 15.8% in 20 sessions into that split with no company news since the 2026-08-20 earnings-date notice.
findings.adversary_note: The central evidence is a sentence management said aloud on the June 8 call - 'the cost is all in Q1... very little of the revenue was in Q1' - which is public by construction and was carried verbatim in the Motley Fool/Globe and Mail transcript plus every earnings recap. The favourable cost-then-revenue split across the Q1/Q2 boundary is therefore the obvious, publicly telegraphed setup for exactly this print; it is the consensus bull framing, not hidden. The claim's own 'market sold the stock 15.8% with no company news' is weak evidence of mispricing: the 20-session decline is far better explained by the 5.56m-share/$94m dilution priced June 29-July 1 (offering struck at $18 vs current $15.37, ~13% dilution) plus digestion of the Q1 miss and small-cap food weakness, not by the market failing to notice a transcript quote it has had for three months.

findings.finding: MAMA raised $94m net at $18.00/share on 2026-06-30 explicitly to fund 'the acquisition of businesses or other assets', has filed no 8-K item 1.01/2.01 in the two months since, and has form for announcing deals into this exact calendar slot: on 2026's equivalent week last year it filed the Crown I asset purchase plus a $20m private placement (8-K dated 2025-09-02, event 2025-08-28) six days before the Q2 print and the stock moved +14.4% that day.
findings.adversary_note: The $94m raise 'to fund the acquisition of businesses or other assets' is fully public and was reported everywhere June 30-July 1 (TipRanks, Globe and Mail, StockTitan, TradingView); the market plainly knows MAMA has M&A firepower and an acquisitive posture, and the Crown I precedent is on EDGAR. So the dry-powder/intent is priced. What is not priced is a specific, unannounced deal landing in this calendar slot - but that is unpriceable by nature rather than missed, and its mechanism to THIS print is speculative: an acquisition is a separate 8-K item 1.01/2.01 that may or may not coincide with the earnings date. The claim leans on low option open interest as evidence the optionality is unpriced, but on a chain with only 526 total contracts and a 55%-of-mid ATM spread, low OI means nobody trades these options at all - not that the market formed and dismissed an M&A view. I therefore read the dead chain as no evidence either way, not as confirmation of hidden upside.

findings.finding: The one customer-side datapoint published after MAMA last spoke cuts the other way: Albertsons on 2026-07-23 cut its FY2026 identical-sales outlook from 0.0%-1.0% to (1.5)%-(0.5)% and cut EBITDA guidance, reporting identical sales -0.8% for the 16 weeks ended 2026-06-20 and citing 'core grocery... increasing pressure from softer industry unit trends and a more cautious consumer' - a window that sits inside MAMA's May-July fiscal Q2, on a company whose banners are perimeter-deli customers.
findings.adversary_note: The Albertsons datapoint is fully public and heavily covered - the July 23 guidance cut (FY ID-sales to -1.5%/-0.5%, EBITDA to $3.55-3.625bn, -0.8% comps for the 16 weeks ended June 20) ran in Drug Store News, Shelby Report, Motley Fool and Albertsons' own release the same day. So the raw fact is priced into ACI and into the broadly-known 'cautious consumer' theme that already sits on small-cap food names. The MAMA read-through is nowhere drawn out explicitly, so that inference is unpriced - but it is weak in magnitude: MAMA grew Q1 revenue 49.7% on new-door rollout (Walmart 2,000 / Target 750 / Food Lion), which is distribution-driven, and a single perimeter customer's -0.8% same-store drift is immaterial against ~50% idiosyncratic growth. The bearish mechanism barely reaches this print.

findings.finding: Hanwha Vision - which signed an $800m+, 10-year, multi-generation edge-AI SoC LTA with Ambarella on 2026-05-28 - reported its security segment's best quarter ever for calendar Q2 2026 (KRW 394.6bn, +20.1% YoY vs KRW 328.4bn), with AI-CCTV rising to 59% of network-camera revenue from 46% a year earlier; that AI mix shift is exactly the content-per-camera driver behind Ambarella's professional IoT line, which is ~75% of its revenue.
findings.adversary_note: The load-bearing fact is published in two places: the Hanwha Vision Q2 result itself carried an English wire item (RTTNews, 'Hanwha Vision Q2 Operating Income, Sales Rise'), and the $800m+/10-year multi-generation LTA was a globenewswire press release on 2026-05-28 covered by Investing.com, StreetInsider, StockTitan and Insider Monkey the same day. What is genuinely obscure is only the segment detail (KRW 394.6bn, AI-CCTV 59% of network-camera revenue) in the Korean-language Herald piece. Against that, two things blunt the mechanism. First, Hanwha Vision's own press release states it retains control of its proprietary Wisenet SoC, so the AI-mix shift inside its calendar-Q2 network-camera revenue is not straightforwardly Ambarella silicon; the LTA is forward, multi-generation revenue and cannot be a material contributor to a quarter that ended 31-Jul-26. Second, Hanwha's Apr-Jun quarter sits inside the window Ambarella itself had visibility on when it guided $105.0-111.0m on 2026-05-28, so the datapoint is confirmatory of the guide rather than incremental to it. And 'AI mix shift raises content per camera in professional IoT' is not a discovery: it is the stated bull case in every Ambarella release and in the sell-side notes (Needham, Morgan Stanley, Rosenblatt all publish it). A customer read-across of unquantified size against a 14% implied move is small.

findings.finding: The baseline's -20.07% 20-day run-up is not a fundamental de-rate: AMBA closed $69.19 on 2026-07-29, jumped +7.08% to $74.09 on 30 July and +16.08% to $86.00 on 31 July on the FT report of NXP takeover talks, and has since bled straight back to $65.43 - only 5.4% below the last undisturbed pre-rumour close, against SMH -6.6% from 7 August to 3 September. There has been no report anywhere that the NXP process ended.
findings.adversary_note: This is a re-reading of the baseline's own run_up field, and every input to it is wire copy or the public tape. The FT report was carried by Reuters, Yahoo Finance, Investing.com, StreetInsider and StocksToTrade on 2026-07-31; the +7.08% and +16.08% days and the subsequent bleed are on the free stockanalysis.com history the hunter itself cites. The market does not need to be told why its own price spiked and faded. More importantly, the reinterpretation is partly wrong on its own arithmetic: the -5.4%-vs-SMH--6.6% comparison mismatches windows, taking AMBA from its pre-rumour 29-Jul close ($69.19) but SMH from its 7-Aug peak ($582.70). On a matched window, SMH went 504.22 on 29-Jul to 544.39 on 3-Sep, i.e. +8.0%, against AMBA -5.4% — about 13.4 points of relative underperformance measured from the undisturbed pre-rumour base, which is the opposite of 'in line with the sector'. From 17-Aug the stock ran roughly 2x the sector's decline (AMBA -16%, SMH -8.4%), consistent with a high-beta de-rate plus premium decay rather than with the benign reading. The one residual that is real and not stated in the baseline is that ~two-thirds of the -20.07% run-up field is rumour-premium decay, so the field should not be read as 'bad news leaking'. That is a correction to our pipeline's reading, not information the market lacks, and it reaches tonight only through the reaction function (a live bidder cushions a bad print), not through the numbers.

findings.finding: Ambarella cut total manufacturing purchase commitments 33% sequentially, from $80.4m at 31-Jan-26 to $53.9m at 30-Apr-26, and booked a first-ever $1.2m adverse-purchase-commitment loss liability (it was exactly $0 the prior quarter) - while inventory rose 54% to $80.4m and days of inventory went 99 to 145, a build management told the call was precautionary against a second-half supply shortage.
findings.adversary_note: Every figure here is in the 10-Q filed 2026-06-02 and the associated release, and the interpretation was supplied publicly by management on the 28-May call, which the finding itself concedes. StockTitan's filing summary published on 2026-06-02 already tied the margin miss to the same line item — 'Gross margin slipped to 58.4%, mainly from higher manufacturing costs and adverse purchase commitments' — and flagged the $25.6m operating cash outflow 'largely due to inventory build'. The bearish inference is also close to self-cancelling: purchase commitments fall when the wafers have already been taken into inventory, and inventory rose 54% in the same quarter, so a 33% sequential decline in open commitments is the arithmetic complement of the build rather than an order cut. Size is small on the company's own numbers: the first-ever adverse-commitment loss is $1.2m against ~$100m quarterly revenue, and total open commitments of $53.9m are about half a quarter of cost of revenue. Management then guided non-GAAP gross margin UP to 59.0-60.5% from 58.4% actual, which is a public statement that they do not expect the commitment problem to widen. Finally the data is as of 30-Apr-26 and tonight's print supersedes it outright.

findings.finding: A customer development project funded by a $13.5m cash advance was terminated on 12-May-26; $4.5m is refunded and the remaining $9.0m is XBRL-tagged as a forecast reduction of R&D expense in the quarter ended 31-Jul-26 - i.e. tonight's quarter - yet the 28-May press release and the earnings call both omitted it entirely while guiding Q2 non-GAAP opex to $56.0-59.0m against $56.4m actual in Q1.
findings.adversary_note: The implication the hunter says nobody drew was drawn, in plain English, on a mainstream retail filing-summary site the day the 10-Q hit: StockTitan on 2026-06-02 wrote that Ambarella 'terminated a development project on May 12, 2026 and agreed to refund $4.5 million of a prior $13.5 million customer deposit, with the remaining $9.0 million to be recognized as a reduction of research and development expense in the next quarter', and explicitly noted that the next quarter is the one ending 31-Jul-26. So this is not an XBRL-only fact; it is a published, correctly-interpreted subsequent-events disclosure three months old. Worse for the claim, the timing cuts against it: the termination was 12-May-26, sixteen days BEFORE the 28-May guide. Management set non-GAAP opex of $56.0-59.0m knowing the credit was coming. Either the credit is inside that guide — in which case consensus, which anchors to Ambarella's opex range, already has it and it is fully priced — or it is not, which would require underlying opex of $65-68m (+16-21% sequentially, far outside this company's history) and therefore implies the company plans to treat the $9.0m as a non-GAAP exclusion, in which case it never touches the non-GAAP EPS the stock actually trades on and only shrinks a GAAP loss that was $18.1m last quarter. Both branches defeat 'unpriced EPS beat'. What survives is modest: that no published preview mentions it, and that if it does land in non-GAAP it is ~$0.20 a share against a ~$0.11-0.15 base, which sell-side would immediately back out as one-time.

findings.finding: The stock at $65.43 is 5.4% BELOW its pre-rumour close of $69.19 on 29-Jul-26, i.e. the entire premium from the FT's 31-Jul-26 report that NXP was in talks to buy the company for over $3bn has been erased and then some, with no report anywhere that the talks collapsed - and the -20.1% 20-session slide compares with only -6.8% for SOXX over the same span, so ~13 points of it is idiosyncratic and unattributed to any dated company news.
findings.adversary_note: This is the price itself. 'The premium is gone and nothing was announced' is a statement about the closing print, observable by anyone on the free tape the sibling finding cites, and the underlying deal report was Reuters/FT wire copy on 2026-07-31 that itself said the talks could collapse. The attribution step is also weaker than stated: the finding calls ~13 points 'unattributed to any dated company news' while measuring from 5-Aug ($81.85), a level that only existed because of the 31-Jul FT report — so a large part of that residual IS dated company news, namely the decay of that report. Separately, from 17-Aug to 3-Sep AMBA fell 16% against SMH -8.4% (594.07 to 544.39), roughly 2x beta on a sector drawdown, which explains much of the rest without any hidden company event. I searched for a dated explanation of the 17-Aug-to-3-Sep slide and found none — no downgrade (Needham raised to $100, Morgan Stanley to $96, Rosenblatt reiterated Buy $120 on 31-Aug), no company release, no report the process ended — so the honest reading is beta plus premium decay plus a pre-print de-rate on a name that has fallen on five of its last seven prints, not information leakage. Unexplained relative weakness into a print on a heavily-covered small cap is the most public observation available and put/call OI of 2.14 shows the option market already leaning the same way.

findings.finding: Tonight's 10-Q is the first Domo filing issued after the deal was signed (7/22), HSR early-terminated (8/25) and the close pulled forward to end-September with no financing condition - which under ASC 205-40 gives management a strong basis to remove the 'substantial doubt exists about the Company's ability to continue as a going concern' language carried in the Q1 10-Q, a machine-readable flag change arriving with no press release or call to dilute it.
findings.adversary_note: Every fact that would justify removing the going-concern qualifier is already public and already carried in the price. HSR early termination (8/25), the pull-forward to an end-September close, and the absence of a financing condition are all disclosed in 8-Ks and in the 8/26 timing press release; the $400M/$4.84-per-share net-cash outcome was announced 7/22 and the stock rose ~21% that day. Removing the ASC 205-40 doubt language is a mechanical accounting consequence of those already-known facts, not new information. A stub trading at $3.815 against a stated $4.84 net-cash-at-close is priced on deal-arbitrage math, where a going-concern flag is second-order; the qualifier existed only because of the covenant/forbearance stress that the signed, HSR-cleared, unconditioned deal resolves — and the market already knows the deal resolves it. The 'machine-readable flag, no PR to dilute it' angle is the only genuinely unpriced sliver, plus residual uncertainty over whether management actually removes it in a filing nobody parses in real time.

findings.finding: Domo paid ~$5.9m of cash lender and legal fees on effectiveness of the June 12 forbearance - i.e. inside the quarter being reported tonight - against cash of $39.1m at 4/30, while the purchase price is '$400m minus the amount, if any, by which $25 million (the Minimum Cash Amount) exceeds our estimation' of cash, with 'no upward adjustment' for cash above $25m; so the 7/31 cash line lands in a narrow corridor where a shortfall cuts proceeds dollar-for-dollar and an excess is transferred to Progress for free.
findings.adversary_note: Both load-bearing components are already published. The ~$5.9M of lender/legal fees on the June 12 forbearance effectiveness are disclosed in the June forbearance 8-K and the Q1 10-Q, and the $39.1M 4/30 cash line is in that same Q1 10-Q. The purchase-price-adjustment formula — $400M base minus the amount by which the $25M Minimum Cash Amount exceeds estimated cash, with no upward adjustment for excess cash — is spelled out in the 8/24 DEFM14C, and the 7/22 announcement itself flagged the price as 'subject to customary purchase price adjustments.' So the mechanism that cash burn can cut shareholder proceeds is public, and the 21% discount of spot ($3.815) to the stated $4.84 net-cash figure already prices deal-value uncertainty of this kind. What is genuinely new tonight is only the exact 7/31 cash snapshot, and even that is not the operative measurement — the adjustment is struck at closing (end-September), not at 7/31 — so a single quarter-end balance-sheet line is a waypoint, not the settlement number. The 'narrow corridor' framing is also somewhat overstated: $39.1M less $5.9M is $33.2M before operating burn, comfortably above the $25M floor at quarter start.

findings.finding: lululemon's Q2 and FY26 guidance was set on 4 June 2026 and the release states it rests on 'management's expectations as of the date of this press release' - but the Great Wall drum crisis only went viral 11-13 days later (>50m Weibo views by 15 June, company apology 16-17 June), i.e. with roughly 7 of Q2's 13 weeks still to run, in the single segment (China Mainland, +30% revenue / +20% comp in Q1) that carries the entire growth story.
findings.adversary_note: This is the single most-covered narrative on the print, and the guidance-vintage nuance does not survive the fact that the affected segment has already been visibly re-marked. Piper Sandler warned China 'could come in softer' after the Great Wall activation; Citi models China at +6.0% versus +12.9% consensus (less than half); BTIG polled consumers on the drum incident specifically and found meaningful impact on brand perception and purchase intent. So the exact mechanism the claim invokes — a June-viral event landing in a China segment the 4-June guide could not contain — has been explicitly priced by multiple brokers via segment-level cuts, not merely alluded to. The residual is only the gap between the market's already-lowered China number and whatever the actual print shows; the direction and cause are consensus.

findings.finding: Alo Yoga opened its Tmall flagship on 12 August 2026 and did RMB 10m (~$1.4m) of sales in the first minute - a record opening day for a new brand in Tmall's sports and outdoor category - after entering mainland China in June 2026 via WeChat and Xiaohongshu with K-pop star Ningning as ambassador.
findings.adversary_note: The Alo Tmall launch was reported the same day across SCMP, China Daily, Yahoo Finance and retail trade press, including the RMB 10m-in-one-minute record — the exact figure the claim cites is in the wire copy, and 'competition mounts' is literally a pre-print headline. More importantly the mechanism barely reaches THIS print: Alo's 12-August launch is a Q3 event and measures Alo's own sales, not lululemon's Q2 China revenue, which is the number reporting today. The competitive-erosion theme is a well-documented structural narrative, not a Q2 datapoint; its effect on the September-3 print is close to nil, so what is 'unpriced' is a slow-burn threat the market already discusses openly.

findings.finding: Chip Wilson, an 8.7% holder who spent 2025-2026 publicly attacking the board and running a proxy fight, has been bound since 26 May 2026 by an ~18-month standstill and non-disparagement covenant running to 30 days before the 2028 nomination deadline - so this is the first LULU earnings print in over two years at which he cannot amplify a bad number the next morning.
findings.adversary_note: The settlement and its 18-month standstill/non-disparagement covenant were reported by CNN, CNBC, Reuters and Retail Dive on 27 May, and CNN's headline is literally 'founder promises not to trash the brand for 18 months' — the exact mechanism the bullish claim rests on is the wire copy. The underlying fact is 100% public and structural; the only novel element is the framing that this is 'the first print where he cannot amplify a bad number,' which is an inference from a known covenant, not new information. As a bullish claim the magnitude is negligible and unquantifiable: the absence of a next-morning critical tweet does not change the fundamentals the print reveals, and a heavily-covered settlement is priced. This is agreement with the record, not an edge.

findings.finding: The Strait of Hormuz shipping crisis worsened sharply during Quanex's exact Q3 window (May-July 2026) - the conflict resumed in July and transits collapsed to roughly 5% of pre-war levels by August - directly undermining the 'rate of inflationary pressure subsides' assumption that management baked into the Q3 revenue/margin outlook when they gave it on June 4.
findings.adversary_note: The underlying driver of this claim is thoroughly public and management has already connected it to its own margins. In the June 4 Q2 release, Quanex explicitly attributed margin pressure to 'the ongoing conflict in the Middle East' and stated its recovery assumption depended on 'the rate of inflationary pressure subsides' — and the stock fell -13.42% that day. The Strait of Hormuz disruption has been globally reported since February 2026 (traffic collapsed to ~5 vessels/day by March 2), and energy prices reflect it across all markets. The July 14 re-escalation and the 95% collapse (July 15-Aug 23) came mostly AFTER Quanex's Q3 window closed on July 31, so the direct Q3-actuals impact is small; input-cost lags mean Q3 COGS reflects earlier-purchased resin. The incremental, unpriced part — 'Hormuz specifically worsened in the exact window and hits NX' — is a narrative overlay on a driver management already named, and its bite lands mostly in Q4 and forward guidance, not the reported quarter.

findings.finding: Quanex's leverage cushion is thin (3.1x net-debt/LTM-EBITDA at 4/30/26 against a 3.25x covenant that tightened from 3.75x this fiscal year), and the strong Q3 2025 quarter ($70.3M adj EBITDA) rolls OUT of the LTM denominator this print while Q3 2026 price-cost recovery is by management's own account incomplete until Q4 - so the ratio can tick UP toward the covenant in Q3 before the Q4 improvement they are guiding to.
findings.adversary_note: Every building block of this claim is already public: the 3.1x leverage at 4/30/26 is stated in the June 4 release and flagged as 'the basis for a key covenant'; the covenant step-down to 3.25x from 3.75x starting Q1 FY2026 is in the amended credit agreement; and the rising trajectory (2.8x at Jan 31 -> 3.1x at Apr 30) is visible in the filings. Multiple pre-print writeups already frame NX around 'high leverage post-acquisition impacting financial flexibility.' So a reader can already see leverage sitting only 0.15x below covenant and trending up. The genuinely less-priced sliver is the EBITDA-roll arithmetic (strong Q3'25 ~$70.3M leaving LTM as a weaker Q3'26 enters) pushing the ratio toward the covenant — plausibly unmodeled given the single published estimate. But management has publicly guided to REDUCING leverage by year-end, and Q3/Q4 are the seasonal cash-generation window, so the net-debt numerator likely falls and partly offsets the falling EBITDA denominator. Whether the ratio actually ticks up, stays flat, or falls is contested, not established, and a proximity-to-covenant (not a breach) carries limited incremental price impact on a name already sold off on leverage.

findings.finding: Planet's remaining performance obligations FELL sequentially last quarter - $852.4M at 2026-01-31 to $816.0M at 2026-04-30, a $36.4M decline against $94.2M of revenue recognised, i.e. RPO book-to-bill of roughly 0.6 - and the May-July quarter now being reported contains no announced nine-figure booking at all, only two seven-figure deals (Scottish Government, 30 Jul; a European defence customer PR'd 9:01am today), so a second consecutive sequential RPO decline is likely while the headline still shows a large YoY gain.
findings.adversary_note: Both halves of the arithmetic are company wire-release figures, not obscure data. $852.4M RPO at 2026-01-31 was in the 2026-03-19 FY26 release (and repeated verbatim in trade coverage), and $816M at 2026-04-30 was in the 2026-06-04 Q1 FY27 release and spoken aloud on the call. The subtraction is trivial and available to anyone who read both press releases; what is genuinely unreported is the framing 'RPO book-to-bill 0.6'. But the forward limb of the claim - that the May-July quarter contains 'no announced nine-figure booking at all, only two seven-figure deals' - is factually wrong as an enumeration: Planet press-released an 8-figure, $22M NGA Luno B option-year extension plus a new NGA/DIU Global Monitoring Service award on 2026-06-04, inside the 1 May - 31 July window, and it was picked up by Defense Daily and Via Satellite the same day. The hunter also selects the one book metric that fell and ignores the one management actually guides on: backlog rose $900M -> $906M over the same quarter, i.e. total bookings roughly matched revenue rather than collapsing to 0.6x. RPO for this name is lumpy by construction (it was +106% YoY at FY26 end on the German/NATO-type multi-year awards), so one $36M sequential draw is not evidence of demand deceleration and the magnitude is genuinely contested. Discounted heavily for the published inputs and the broken forward premise; credited for the fact that no preview or sell-side note frames this quarter as a bookings problem.

findings.finding: Planet's own Q3 FY26 release states the NRO renewed its baseline EOCL contract for PlanetScope broad-area monitoring for $13.2M 'through June 2026' - so Planet's anchor US intelligence contract expired inside the quarter just reported, and no renewal has been announced anywhere in the June-September 2026 window even though Planet press-released two seven-figure European deals in that same window.
findings.source_date: 2025-12-10 (date confirmed from the URL path segment 20251210)
findings.adversary_note: The load-bearing fact is a line in Planet's own Q3 FY26 wire release on 2025-12-10 - the URL path segment 20251210 confirms the year, so this is a prior-fiscal-year document, not a fresh one - and it was reproduced by Intelligence Community News and the trade press at the time. 'Anchor US intelligence contract with an expiry inside the next few quarters' is therefore in the wire copy, and EOCL budget risk for the commercial EO operators is one of the most worn narratives in the sector after BlackSky's publicly reported EOCL revenue gap. Two things then cut the residual hard. First, the absence of a renewal press release is close to worthless as evidence: Planet has never press-released a baseline EOCL renewal as a standalone item - the December 2025 renewal itself was disclosed only inside the quarterly release - so 'no PR since June' is exactly what the base rate predicts whether or not the contract renewed. Second, and more damaging, management raised FY27 revenue guidance from $415-440M to $425-441M on 2026-06-04, four weeks before the stated expiry and with full knowledge of it. Either they had renewal visibility or they had already absorbed the loss into the guide; on both branches the guidance the market is marking against already reflects it. Size is real but modest: ~$13.2M for the period, ~$21M annualised, roughly 5% of the FY27 revenue midpoint, against a segment growing 65% YoY. The unpublished residual is the specific observation that the expiry fell inside the quarter now being reported.

findings.finding: FY27 adjusted EBITDA is guided to $0-10M against FY26 actual adjusted EBITDA of $15.5M - profitability guided DOWN while revenue is guided up ~41% - and the EBITDA range has stayed $0-10M through two upward revisions to both revenue ($415-440M to $425-441M) and gross margin (50-52% to 52-54%), which arithmetically requires roughly 30% opex growth; Planet's job board currently carries 114 open requisitions, overwhelmingly quota-bearing sales, pre-sales and customer-success roles in Berlin/Netherlands/UK.
findings.adversary_note: This is published guidance, twice over, and it is the single most-reported thing about this stock in 2026. FY27 adjusted EBITDA of breakeven-to-$10M against FY26 actual $15.5M was issued 2026-03-19 and reaffirmed alongside the revenue and gross-margin raises on 2026-06-04, and it is the stated cause of the -25.98% reaction that day: the wire copy explicitly said the $5M midpoint sat below the $8.23M consensus. Chartmill headlined it 'Revenue Beat Fails to Lift Stock as Guidance Disappoints'; Benzinga and Motley Fool both ran follow-ups on the margin guide-down from 56% to 52-54% plus $80-95M capex. The 2026-09-02 previews are still carrying it forward - 'investors will watch whether growth investments pressure near-term earnings.' The 'arithmetically requires ~30% opex growth' step is inference from published numbers, not new information, and Q1 opex of $85.3M is in the same release. The only genuinely unpublished datum is the 114 open requisitions on the job board, which is a soft proxy with no dollar figure attached and which management has already pre-announced in words ('continue to invest in our global sales and marketing organization'). Under the stated anchors, restating published guidance sits at 90-100; I hold at 90 only for the job-board sliver.

findings.finding: The one thing that has historically broken Planet's satellite-services revenue recognition - launch and delivery slippage - did not happen this quarter: three additional Pelicans launched 2026-05-03 and Pelican-11, the Gen-2 technology demonstrator, launched 2026-07-07 on Transporter-17, both inside the 1 May - 31 July window that the $102-107M guide depends on.
findings.source_date: 2026-05-03 (date confirmed from the URL path segment 20260503)
findings.adversary_note: Attacking the bullish one as hard as the bears: this is the weakest of the four on novelty. Every fact in it was issued by Planet itself on Business Wire and syndicated - the three-Pelican launch on 2026-05-03 (URL segment 20260503 confirms the year), first light including Sweden's first sovereign satellite on 2026-05-14, the Pelican-11 shipment on 2026-06-02, and the Pelican-11 Gen-2 tech-demo launch on Transporter-17 on 2026-07-06/07, with Reuters and TradingView carrying the shipment and launch. Management then guided Q2 FY27 revenue to $102-107M on 2026-06-04, after the May launch had already happened and with Pelican-11 already at Vandenberg, and consensus has settled at $104.1M - dead on the guide midpoint - with analysts reconfirming estimates over the last 30 days. So 'launches did not slip, therefore the $102-107M guide holds' is not a discovery; it is the consensus, restated. The mechanism is also thinner than presented: the large majority of Planet's revenue is recurring data subscription that does not depend on a launch clearing inside the window, and the one line that genuinely does - dedicated satellite services milestone recognition, e.g. the Swedish sovereign satellite - had its launch and first light press-released twelve and one weeks before management set the guide. The residual is only that a market this beaten up may have stopped assuming execution, and there is a sliver of Gen-2 30cm-timeline optionality that is not in any number.
